title: Replacement Level
subtitle: 2026 draft board · pick 5 of 12 · ESPN · Sunday Sept 6

headline_rule.heading: The only number you need to remember

hot.label: worst RB you'll ever have to start

cool.label: worst WR you'll ever have to start

paragraphs: In a 12-team league with one flex, about 34 running backs and 32 receivers start every week. The 34th back projects 137 points; the 32nd receiver projects 165. Every player's value is his projection minus that number — the Surplus column — because the alternative to drafting him is the guy you get for free.

So a receiver is worth 28 points less than his raw projection suggests. Zay Flowers (215) out-projects Breece Hall (203) and Hall is still the better pick by surplus. Tight ends are the exception: Bowers and McBride sit 25 points above the next tier, and ESPN rooms take both in round 2.

pick_notes.5: Running back if Bijan fell (21%). Otherwise Jaxon Smith-Njigba — he and Taylor are a one-point coin flip on surplus, and the WR cliff below JSN is 16 points. Cook if all three are gone.
pick_notes.20: Tight end. Bowers if he's there (52%); McBride if not (72%). The 25-point cliff below them closes before 29. Kyren Williams only if both are gone.
pick_notes.29: Zay Flowers — outside the top five by surplus, first by what's left at 44 (he's gone by then; the tier-4 backs aren't). Kyren Williams over him if he fell (31%). Breece Hall is the safe third. Check Flowers' Friday practice status.
pick_notes.44: Running back. Bucky Irving (71%); Josh Jacobs (60%) is the same tier if Irving is gone. Breece Hall if he somehow fell (23%). Quinshon Judkins and David Montgomery survive to 53 half the time, so don't take them here. Tetairoa McMillan if you went RB at 29.
pick_notes.53: Quarterback. Jayden Daniels if he's there (47%) — in this ESPN room every 340-point QB is gone by 77. Jalen Hurts second (68%). Otherwise a receiver: Jameson Williams, Davante Adams or Terry McLaurin (86–90% there).
pick_notes.77: Running back. Jaylen Warren (90%) — best surplus on the board and the sim's most-owned player. Parker Washington if you still need a WR2. Henderson sat out Thursday (ankle); skip.
pick_notes.92: Mahomes (81% here, 39% at 101) if you still have no quarterback. Otherwise wide receiver: Brian Thomas Jr. (49%), then Alec Pierce or DK Metcalf.
pick_notes.101: Quarterback if you still don't have one: Mahomes (39%), else Dart (75%). Otherwise RB depth — RJ Harvey (15%) or Kenny Gainwell (47%), the Irving handcuff.
pick_notes.116: Nothing above replacement except a TE2 (Kelce 51%, Likely 80%). Kyler Murray is a free QB here (99%). Prefer the second-year names in the late block.
pick_notes.125: Lottery tickets with a path to volume. KC Concepcion (59%), Kyle Monangai if he lasted. Travis Kelce or Isaiah Likely if you skipped TE2.

late_note: Picks 140–173: handcuffs, second-year volume, and next-year keepers. Kicker at 164, defense at 173 — never earlier.
late_body: Claim Samaje Perine (Brown's backup) off waivers Week 1; he won't be drafted. Draft Gainwell (Irving's handcuff, 47% at 101) if you took Irving. Waiver pickups can't be kept in this league, so rounds 12–14 are where you manufacture next year's cheap keeper: Jordyn Tyson (100% at 149), Travis Hunter (100% at 173 — the draft ends before ADP reaches him), Mike Washington (Jeanty's fill-in, 61% at 149), Tank Bigsby (75% at 173). The room starts on kickers and defenses in round 11: Seattle, Denver and Houston are gone by 140; Baltimore (82%) or Buffalo (99%) at 173. Chase McLaughlin (52%) or Cam Little (34%) at 164. Brandon Aubrey (+25 over K12) is gone by 149 (25%) — not worth pick 140 for 1.5 a week.

vegas.text: Chase Brown rushing-yards line (−110), 5.5 rushing TDs (−125), 1,000+ at +210 — Sharp Football, Aug 31. The market's median is 10–20 points below mine. He's still +40 over pick 68 at the book's number.
Bengals win total, under −120 (BetMGM via VegasInsider, Sept 2). A mild negative for a back whose value came partly from pass-catching in shootouts.
Ravens win total, tied-highest in the league with the Rams, over −155. Flowers is the unquestioned WR1 on the best game script in football.
Bo Nix's 2025 pass attempts — most in the NFL — at 6.4 yards per attempt, 28th of 33. The Waddle premise is right about volume and silent about efficiency. Denver's total is 9.5 (over −125).
Waddle receiving-yards prop (Yahoo, Aug 24) — consistent with my 174, not with a WR2 price.
Jaguars (over −140) and Buccaneers (under −135). Jacksonville's offense is real; Tuten gets a third of it. Tampa's is a coin flip with Egbuka's toe.
Falcons win total, over −140, with no starting QB named as of Sept 2. Pitts' target floor is real; the ceiling depends on who throws.
Bears win total, under −125; Caleb Williams over 3,645 passing yards is a featured play. Enough volume for Loveland and Odunze; Burden is the third mouth.

target_note: Across 1,500 simulated drafts the starter total ran 1,772 to 1,906 (mean 1,852); this build projects 1,858 with every pick at least a coin flip. Fallbacks: McBride for Bowers at 20 (72%), Kyren Williams over Flowers at 29 if he fell (31%), Jacobs for Irving at 44 (60%), Jameson Williams for Daniels at 53 (89%) with Mahomes at 92 (81%). The known weakness is RB2 — Irving is a committee back — and the hedge is Kyren at 29 plus McMillan at 44 (66%), which costs nothing if Kyren is there.

terms.def: The score of the worst player at a position who still has to be in someone's starting lineup every week. RB 137, WR 165, TE 114, QB 312 in this league.
Projection minus replacement level. The points a player adds over the player you could have had for free. Every table on this sheet is sorted by it.
How often the player was still undrafted at that pick across 1,500 simulated drafts. Below 50%: plan for him being gone. Above 80%: don't reach.
A tier is a group of players close enough in projection that which one you get barely matters. A cliff is the point drop between tiers — pay before it or wait until after it.

With twelve keepers removed, the player available at a pick is worse than ADP suggests. Measured here: +11 picks at 5, +8 at 20, +6 at 29, +4 at 44, +3 at 53, and under one from 77 on, because twelve picks are forfeited too.
Share of the team's pass plays a player runs a route on; targets per route run; yards per route run. Predictive in that order — YPRR is noise under ~250 routes.

how_built: Projections are mine, built Sept 3, 2026 from 2025 production and 2026 roles, scored in this league's exact settings (0.5 PPR, 4-pt pass TD, −2 INT). Five were changed after research: Egbuka 206→192 (toe, no team drills as of Sept 2), Tuten 200→176 (Coen: 'by committee', Aug 26), Irving 201→188 (Gainwell/Tucker roles), Nabers 207→197 (ACL, Week 1 uncommitted), Jeanty 199→191 (ankle).

ADP: ESPN column of the Footballguys cross-platform table for the top 100 (fetched Sept 3, 2026); FantasyFootballCalculator half-PPR 12-team mocks Aug 28–Sep 2 for the spread and for players beyond the top 100. ESPN rooms take QBs and TEs a round early and let receivers slide 10–17 picks; that is priced in.

Simulation: 1,500 drafts (seed 1000) with twelve keepers drawn (weighted toward better players, keeper rounds correlated to quality), opponents drafting ESPN ADP plus noise scaled to each player's spread and capped, positional need from round 8, kickers and defenses on a rising curve from round 11. Net keeper inflation measured in-sim: +11.2 picks at 5, +7.9 at 20, +6.1 at 29, +3.9 at 44, +2.9 at 53, +0.5 at 77, +0.1 at 92. Replacement ranks QB12 / RB34 / WR32 / TE14. The mock-ADP comparison uses the same simulator on players_mock-adp.csv.
Betting lines: VegasInsider win totals (BetMGM, Sept 2, 2026); season props from Sharp Football Analysis (Aug 31) and Yahoo (Aug 24). Used as a check on medians, never as projections.
News and usage: FantasyPros and RotoWire feeds, FantasyFootballCalculator player-news pages, PFF, Bleacher Nation, Pewter Report, team sites — all fetched Sept 3, 2026, items dated June 9–Sept 3.
assumptions: Starting lineup assumed: 1 QB, 2 RB, 2 WR, 1 TE, 1 RB/WR/TE flex, K, DEF; six bench. No superflex.
Keeper rule assumed: one keeper at the original draft round (same round), waiver pickups not keepable, Brown at round 6. Confirm on the commissioner's sheet before Sunday.
Injuries are baked into expected games, not modeled separately. Re-check Flowers, Egbuka, Nabers, Jeanty, Tuten, Nacua, Chase, Hall and Henderson on Saturday's report.
Kickers and defenses are treated as near-interchangeable and drafted in the last two rounds; the room starts on them in round 11 and the top three defenses are gone by pick 140.
Fifteen rounds means anyone with an ADP past ~155 goes undrafted; late lottery tickets are effectively free.
appendix.flip_warning: The 28-point RB-vs-WR replacement gap. If my tier-3/4 receiver projections are 8–10% low, Flowers at 29 is clearly right and Irving at 44 becomes McMillan; if the backs are the ones under-projected, take Kyren or Hall at 29 without hesitation. Decide which side you're on before the draft, not during it.
appendix.gold_warning: The simulated opponents draft rationally off ESPN ADP. Your actual leaguemates don't — two of them take a QB by round 4 every year — so QBs will go earlier than this sheet says and receivers will fall further. When a tier-3 player is somehow there two rounds late, take him.
